name: music

attributes.attribute: an art and religious symbol in Celtic lands
a lure in fairy tales that draws mortals into enchanted places
an instrument that reached Ireland in medieval times
a song said to come from the fairy world, known as Danny Boy

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Music is an art and a religious symbol in Celtic lands. The music of the ancient Celts is lost to us. The Celts had no written musical notation. We do not know its place in their daily rites. Old writers name horn and string instruments that looked like lyres. Archaeology finds little to confirm this. Some Celtic coins of the Roman age show such instruments. The harp came to Ireland in medieval times. The bagpipe also came late, moving from the Balkans to the insular lands. Singing stayed a valued art. The fairy tales show music as a lure. Otherworld melodies draw mortals into enchanted places. Fairies rewarded good musicians with a tune from Fairyland. The song Derry Aire, known as Danny Boy, was held to come from that world.
